audit.whatIsWrong: Sion's ultimate is called 'Unstoppable Force' in five separate fields (whys[4], spikes[1].text, mid, late, wants.you[2]). Unstoppable Force is MALPHITE's ultimate. Sion's is Unstoppable Onslaught.
audit.why: Kit file lists R as Unstoppable Onslaught. suspectNames is empty because 'Unstoppable Force' is a real, correctly spelled ability name — it just belongs to a different champion, which name-similarity detection cannot catch. This is the same class of error as 'Ares of Blaze' for Pyroclasm, and it is on the page a paying user reads before every Sion game.
audit.corrected: Unstoppable Onslaught: a steerable 7500-range charge that ramps speed and knocks up harder the further it has travelled, on 140/100/60.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fields say Soul Furnace's detonation knocks Sylas back and 'resets the spacing' (whys[2], early, wants.foe[1]).
audit.why: Riot text: 'Sion shields himself and can reactivate after 3 seconds to deal Magic Damage to enemies nearby.' Damage only — no displacement, no flags for knockup or knockback. The real constraint is the opposite of what the page implies: he CANNOT detonate for a full 3 seconds after casting it, which is a window, not a threat.
audit.corrected: Soul Furnace absorbs and then damages on a 15s cooldown with a mandatory 3-second delay. Nothing about it pushes you off him.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[0] calls Decimating Smash's window '8-second', and the late paragraph says your stolen R returns 'every 110 seconds'.
audit.why: Decimating Smash is 10/9/8/7/6 — 10s at rank 1, not 8. Hijack is 80/55/30, never 110. Sion's own R is 140/100/60, so the cooldown story is strongly in your favour and the page understates it.
audit.corrected: Hijack at 80s against Unstoppable Onslaught's 140s means you get his ultimate back nearly twice as often as he does.

audit.why: Both layers read Skill / Sion / Sion / Skill / Skill / Sion / Skill and match the packet chart exactly. The mirror proposed no difficulty-shape change. Sylas 48.52% over 643 games fits a lane he loses at 2-3 and evens out later.

audit.whatIsWrong: Decimating Smash is described as a flat 'charged knockup' with no statement of the condition, and Roar of the Slayer is never named or described at all.
audit.why: Riot text on Q: 'If he charges for enough time, enemies hit by the swing will also be knocked up and stunned' — a short charge is damage and slow only. Roar of the Slayer is 800 range on 12/11/10/9/8, slows and reduces armour, and knocks minions back through the line.
audit.corrected: Making him release the charge early downgrades the whole threat to a slow. His E is the long-range poke and armour shred you actually eat while spacing.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sion.json (Q and E text, ranges, cooldowns)

audit.whatIsWrong: The 'zombie passive' is mentioned as flavour but never as a mechanic that changes your itemisation or your kill timing.
audit.why: Glory in Death: his reanimated attacks are very rapid, HEAL him, and deal bonus damage based on the target's MAXIMUM health. So killing him starts a second fight, HP stacking makes you a better target, and Grievous Wounds needs to be on him before he dies, not after.
audit.corrected: Land anti-heal before the kill, and do not answer him by stacking health.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sion.json (P text, heal and percentHealth flags)

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeBad and dontsFull refer to Sylas losing 'no stun'.
audit.why: Riot's Abscond/Abduct text describes a dash and a recast pull; no hardCC flag. The mirror auditor also declined to repeat it, and equally declined to assert the negative.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the real risk — no shield, no gap-close, while Decimating Smash is charging.

edits.before: Stealing Sion's Unstoppable Force turns his primary engage into your engage tool, but his zombie passive and immovable bulk mean he retains teamfight threat even without his R — the window is real but not decisive.
edits.after: Hijacking Unstoppable Onslaught gives you a steerable charge that knocks up harder the further it runs, but Glory in Death still gives him a second life after you kill him — real window, not a decisive one.

edits.before: Steal Sion's Unstoppable Force with your R and immediately look to E-hook him — a charging Sion with no R to disengage is suddenly your target, not your threat.
edits.after: Hijack Unstoppable Onslaught at 80s against his 140s — you get the charge back nearly twice as often, so spend it to start fights he then has no ultimate to answer.

edits.before: Steal his Unstoppable Force at 6 and use it to engage onto HIM — a Sion without his R to force a fight is just a slow melee tank you can bully
edits.after: Hijack Unstoppable Onslaught and charge it INTO him — the knockup scales with distance travelled, so start the charge from far out, not from on top of him

edits.before: Sion's full Q-W-E kit punishes every E approach: he knocks you up, absorbs your W with his own shield detonation, and E-pokes while you recover — your sustain cannot offset the spacing reset.
edits.after: Decimating Smash knocks you up if he holds the charge, Soul Furnace eats your burst and detonates three seconds later, and Roar of the Slayer shreds your armour from 800 — your sustain cannot cover all three.

edits.before: Absorb your W with his own W shield, then knock you back with the detonation to reset the spacing before your heal matters
edits.after: Eat your burst on Soul Furnace, wait the 3 seconds, then detonate it for magic damage while your Kingslayer heal is still on cooldown

edits.before: Hook in with E when Sion's charged Q is on cooldown or not yet charged — that 8-second window is your only safe approach
edits.after: Hook with E when Decimating Smash is down or uncharged — it is 10s at rank 1, and an uncharged swing only damages and slows

edits.before: - Sion Decimating Smash (Stun): matchup-defining — Charged knockup — break the channel or sidestep the slam. It governs your forward steps. - E1 shield spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Sion Decimating Smash: matchup-defining — 10s at rank 1, and only the fully charged swing knocks up; a short one just damages and slows. - Soul Furnace is 15s and cannot detonate for 3 seconds. - Unstoppable Onslaught is 140s against your 80s Hijack.

edits.before: Charged knockup — break the channel or sidestep the slam. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Only a fully charged Decimating Smash knocks up — make him release it early and it is a slow you walk out of.

edits.before: Track Sion’s Decimating Smash (Stun): Charged knockup — break the channel or sidestep the slam. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Track Sion’s Glory in Death: killing him starts a second life whose autos heal him off your max health, so land Grievous Wounds before he drops.

edits.before: Engaging with both E charges spent — no shield, no stun, and you're a melee mage standing in the open.
edits.after: Engaging with both E charges spent — no shield, no gap-close, and Decimating Smash is still charging.

edits.before: Both E charges spent means no shield and no exit — you're a melee mage in the open.
edits.after: The knockup is only on the long charge — sidestep the wind-up and it is a slow.

edits.before: Engaging with both E charges spent — no shield, no stun, and you're a melee mage standing in the open.
edits.after: Unstoppable Onslaught steers and travels 7500 — a stolen one reaches fights two lanes away from you.

notes: The headline error: five fields called Sion's ultimate 'Unstoppable Force', which is Malphite's ability. The defect scanner missed it because the string is a real, correctly spelled ability name attached to the wrong champion — worth flagging to whoever tunes suspectNames, since edit-distance checks are structurally blind to this. Second: three fields claimed Soul Furnace's detonation knocks Sylas back; Riot's text has no displacement at all, and the ability's real quirk is that it cannot be detonated for 3 seconds. Two errors I could not reach inside the length band and that want a sweep: the 'late' paragraph says the stolen R returns 'every 110 seconds' (Hijack is 80/55/30), and the mid and late paragraphs both refer to layering 'your E stun', repeating the Abscond/Abduct stun invention the mirror auditor flagged.
